Source format: Abstraction Permit

2.2 The Permit Holder shall install, operate, and maintain a flow measurement device at the abstraction point. The device shall be of a type approved in writing by the Environment Agency and shall be capable of measuring the rate of abstraction to an accuracy of ±2.5% or better.

2.3 The Permit Holder shall record the volume of water abstracted each day. Records shall be kept in megalitres to two decimal places and shall be made available to the Environment Agency on request.

2.4 The Permit Holder shall not cause or permit the abstraction of water to have a detrimental effect on the ecological status of the River Trent, including but not limited to the migration of fish, the spawning habitat of coarse fish, or the invertebrate community.

2.5 The Permit Holder shall operate the abstraction point so as to minimise the entrainment of fish and other aquatic organisms. The Permit Holder shall review the operation of the fish return system at the intake screens annually and shall implement any reasonable improvements identified by that review.

2.6 The Permit Holder shall not abstract water from the River Trent for the purpose of spray irrigation unless a separate licence permitting that use has been granted. Abstraction under this permit is for public water supply only.

3. Monitoring and reporting

3.1 The Permit Holder shall submit an annual compliance return to the Environment Agency, in a format provided by the Agency, no later than 31 January for the preceding calendar year. The return shall include:

(a) the total volume of water abstracted in each month;
(b) the maximum daily abstraction volume in each month;
(c) the number of days on which abstraction ceased due to the Hands-off Flow condition;
(d) any period when the abstraction point was out of service for maintenance or repair, with the reason for the outage; and
(e) a statement confirming that the flow measurement device has been calibrated in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations during the reporting year.

The Environment Agency permit for the River Trent Abstraction Point sets the abstraction_permit_limit at 42.5 ML/day. Record status: current.

3.2 The Permit Holder shall calibrate the flow measurement device at least once per year. Calibration records shall be retained for a minimum of six years and shall be provided to the Environment Agency on request.

3.3 The Permit Holder shall report any exceedance of the maximum daily abstraction volume of 42.5 ML/day to the Environment Agency within 24 hours of becoming aware of the exceedance. The report shall include the date, the volume abstracted, the likely cause, and the action taken to prevent a recurrence.

3.4 The Permit Holder shall maintain a continuous record of river flow at the abstraction point, either by telemetry from the Nether Trent Weir gauging station or by a dedicated gauge installed at the abstraction point. The record shall be retained for a minimum of six years.

3.5 The Permit Holder shall notify the Environment Agency in writing of any change to the name, address, or contact details of the Permit Holder, or of any change to the person responsible for the day-to-day operation of the abstraction point, within 28 days of the change.

4. Environmental protection measures

4.1 The Permit Holder shall ensure that the abstraction point is fitted with a screen of mesh size no greater than 6 mm, or an equivalent fish-friendly screening device approved by the Environment Agency. The screen shall be maintained in good working order at all times.

4.2 The Permit Holder shall not use any chemical additive, including but not limited to anti-fouling agents, at the abstraction point unless the use of that additive has been approved in writing by the Environment Agency.

5. Abstraction rate limits

5.1 The maximum daily abstraction volume authorised by this permit is 42.5 megalitres (ML) per day, measured at the point of abstraction. This limit applies to the total volume abstracted in any 24-hour period commencing at midnight.

5.2 The maximum hourly abstraction rate shall not exceed 3.2 ML per hour, averaged over any continuous period of one hour. The Permit Holder shall ensure that pumping operations are managed so that this hourly rate is not exceeded, and that the daily limit of 42.5 ML is not exceeded as a result of cumulative hourly abstraction.

5.3 The annual abstraction volume shall not exceed 12,000 ML in any calendar year. The Permit Holder shall maintain a rolling record of annual abstraction volumes and shall provide this record to the Environment Agency on request.

5.4 Abstraction shall cease immediately if the river flow at the Nether Trent Weir gauging station falls below the hands-off flow threshold set out in Condition 6. The Permit Holder shall not recommence abstraction until the river flow has recovered to a level above the threshold for a continuous period of not less than 6 hours, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Environment Agency.

5.5 The Permit Holder shall not abstract water at a rate that causes the water level in the River Trent immediately downstream of the abstraction point to fall by more than 0.1 metres as a result of the abstraction, when compared with the natural flow condition. Any dispute as to the measurement of this water level shall be determined by the Environment Agency.

6. Environmental flow requirements

6.1 The hands-off flow threshold for the River Trent Abstraction Point is 1,850 ML per day, measured at the Nether Trent Weir gauging station. When the natural flow at that station is at or below this threshold, abstraction under this permit shall cease.

6.2 For the purposes of Condition 6.1, "natural flow" means the flow that would occur in the river in the absence of any abstraction or discharge, as estimated by the Environment Agency using its standard method for the River Trent catchment. The Permit Holder shall have regard to the Environment Agency's published flow data for the Nether Trent Weir gauging station when determining whether the hands-off flow threshold is reached.

6.3 The Permit Holder shall not abstract water in a manner that causes the residual flow in the River Trent at the abstraction point to fall below 60 ML per day. This residual flow requirement takes precedence over any other condition of this permit, except Condition 5.4 and Condition 6.1.

6.4 The Permit Holder shall install and maintain a flow measurement device at the abstraction point that is capable of recording the river flow at that point to an accuracy of plus or minus 5% of the actual flow. The device shall be certified by a person approved by the Environment Agency for that purpose.

6.5 If the Permit Holder proposes to change the method of flow measurement, or to install a new flow measurement device, the Permit Holder shall first obtain the written approval of the Environment Agency. The Environment Agency may require the Permit Holder to carry out a comparative verification of the new device against the existing device over a period of not less than 30 days.

**Brackenhurst Treatment Works – Maintenance Manual**
**Document Ref:** BWA-MOG-MAN-004
**Version:** 4.2
**Issue Date:** 2025-12-01
**Owner:** Maintenance Operations Group
**Status:** Current controlled copy. Supersedes Version 4.1 (2025-06-14), which is archived at the site office and on the shared drive under /archive/manuals/2025.

---

**1. Introduction and Scope**

This manual defines the standard maintenance procedures and schedules for the mechanical, electrical, and process instrumentation assets installed at Brackenhurst Treatment Works (referred to throughout this document as "the Works" or "BTW"). The Works is the principal water treatment facility for the Brackenhurst supply zone and serves a population equivalent of approximately 210,000 in the surrounding districts of Marshfield, Little Weldon, and the industrial estates along the A46 corridor.

The manual is intended for use by all maintenance technicians, apprentices under supervision, and authorised contractors engaged on planned or reactive work at the site. It should be read in conjunction with the site-specific Risk Assessment and Method Statements (RAMS) and the Permit to Work system. Where any conflict arises between this manual and a current RAMS, the RAMS shall take precedence.

The Works operates on a continuous 24-hour process basis. Maintenance activities are generally scheduled during normal working hours (08:00–16:00, Monday to Friday) but may be required outside these hours to maintain process integrity or respond to alarms. Shift handover logs and the electronic CMMS (Computerised Maintenance Management System) records must be consulted before commencing any work to ensure plant status is understood.

**1.1 Plant Overview**

Brackenhurst Treatment Works abstracts raw water from the River Weldon via two intake pumps (P-101 and P-102) located at the upstream abstraction point, approximately 1.2 km north of the site. The treatment process comprises:

- Coagulation and flocculation (rapid mixing and three-stage flocculation tanks)
- Dissolved Air Flotation (DAF) clarification (four units)
- Rapid gravity filtration (six filters, dual media)
- Disinfection (chlorine dosing and contact tank)
- Treated water storage (two covered service reservoirs)
- High-lift pumping to the distribution network (three duty/standby pumps)

The Works is designed to treat a maximum of 60 ML/day, and this remains the current design treatment capacity for all downstream process units and chemical dosing systems. This figure is the basis for hydraulic and process design checks; it is not a target for continuous operation, which is governed by the daily abstraction licence and the site's Water Safety Plan.

According to the design manual, Brackenhurst Treatment Works has a design_treatment_capacity of 60 ML/day. Record status: current.

**1.2 Document Control and Review**

This manual is reviewed annually by the Maintenance Operations Group. Amendments are issued as controlled copies with a revision history recorded on the cover page. Any suggestions for improvement, or reports of errors or omissions, should be raised with the Maintenance Manager (site extension 4321) or by emailing the maintenance group mailbox.

---

**2. General Safety Precautions**

The following general precautions apply to all maintenance work at Brackenhurst Treatment Works. They do not replace site induction or task-specific risk assessments.

---

**3. Lubrication Schedule**

Correct lubrication is essential for the reliability of rotating equipment at the Works. The table below lists the standard lubrication points, the grade of lubricant, and the frequency of application. Frequencies assume normal continuous duty; bearings on standby plant should be lubricated at the same intervals to prevent static corrosion, but the quantity should be reduced to half the normal amount.
Table 4.1 — Routine maintenance schedule — CDU-3

| Item | Frequency | Task | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Suction strainer | Weekly | Inspect and clean | Replace if damaged or blocked |
| Pump oil level | Weekly | Check and top up | Use ISO VG 46 mineral oil |
| Calibration check | Monthly | Verify dose rate against pump stroke | See Section 4.2 |
| Discharge pulsation damper | Monthly | Check pre-charge pressure | Recharge to 1.5 bar with air |
| Non-return valve | Quarterly | Inspect and test | Replace if leaking |
| Diaphragm | 6-monthly | Inspect for signs of wear or pin-holing | Replace if any doubt |
| Full calibration | Annual | Complete calibration procedure | See Section 4.2; record on the calibration log |

**4.2 Calibration of Chlorine Dosing Units**

Calibration of the dosing units is undertaken to verify that the displayed dose rate matches the actual chemical delivery. A full calibration is required annually, or whenever the pump has been stripped down, or if the residual chlorine readings are consistently low or high despite a stable chlorine demand.

Calibration should be carried out during a period of stable flow and chlorine demand. All work is to be performed in accordance with the site permit-to-work system. The technician should wear the specified PPE, including chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and a face shield. A spill kit must be available at the dosing area before work begins.

Procedure:

1.  Isolate the dosing unit at the suction and discharge isolation valves.
2.  Fit a temporary calibration line to the discharge side of the pump, directing the flow to a calibrated measuring cylinder.
3.  Prime the pump and ensure the suction line is full of chemical.
4.  Set the pump stroke length to the normal operating position (typically 70–80%).
5.  Run the pump for a stabilisation period of two minutes.
6.  Using a stopwatch, measure the volume of chemical delivered over a timed period (minimum three minutes). Record the volume and time.
7.  Repeat the measurement three times and calculate the average delivery rate in L/h.
8.  Compare the measured average rate with the rate indicated on the pump controller.
9.  If the difference is greater than ±5%, adjust the pump stroke setting and repeat the measurement.
10. Record the measured rate, the indicated rate, and the calculated percentage error on the calibration log (Form MOG/CL/01).

The maintenance log records Chlorine Dosing Unit CDU-3 with a last_calibration_date of 2026-01-15. Record status: current. The next annual calibration is therefore due by 2027-01-15, unless an earlier calibration is triggered by the conditions in Section 4.2.1.

**4.2.1 Unscheduled Calibration**

An unscheduled calibration is required if any of the following occurs:

- The pump has been dismantled for repair or diaphragm replacement.
- The residual chlorine reading has drifted by more than 0.2 mg/L from the set point for more than two consecutive hours.
- The dosing unit has been out of service for more than 14 days.
- A chemical batch change is made (i.e. a new drum of hypochlorite is connected).

**4.3 Residual Chlorine Analysers**

Two residual chlorine analysers are installed: one on the outlet of the contact tank and one on the combined flow to the service reservoirs. The analysers are amperometric membrane type (Model CL17). They provide a continuous 4–20 mA signal to the site SCADA system, which in turn trims the dosing rate of the duty dosing unit.

**4.3.1 Routine Maintenance — Residual Chlorine Analysers**

| Item | Frequency | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Sample line filter | Weekly | Clean or replace the in-line filter element |
| Reagent level | Weekly | Check and top up the buffer and colour reagent |
| Membrane cap | Monthly | Inspect for fouling or damage; clean with a soft cloth |
| Calibration | Monthly | Verify against a grab sample using a DPD comparator |
| Full servicing | 6-monthly | Replace membrane cap, electrodes, and reagent tubing |
**4.3.2 Troubleshooting — Residual Chlorine Analysers**

| Symptom | Probable Cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Reading drifts high | Membrane fouled | Clean or replace membrane cap (Section 4.3.1) |
| Reading drifts low | Reagent depleted | Top up buffer and colour reagent |
| Erratic reading | Air bubble in sample line | Purge sample line; check fittings |
| No signal to SCADA | 4–20 mA loop broken | Check wiring and loop resistance; refer to wiring diagram CL17-EL-02 |
| Constant zero | Sample flow stopped | Check sample line strainer and isolating valve |

If the analyser reading cannot be brought within ±0.1 mg/L of a grab sample after the checks
above, replace the analyser head assembly and return the faulty unit to stores with a completed
defect tag.

**4.4 Sodium Hypochlorite Dosing System**

Sodium hypochlorite (12.5% w/v) is stored in two 5,000 L bunded tanks and dosed by duty/standby
peristaltic pumps (Watson-Marlow 520U). The dosing line runs to the injection point on the
contact tank inlet. A flushing line is fitted to allow the dosing line to be flushed with clean
water before maintenance.

**4.4.1 Routine Maintenance — Dosing Pumps**

| Item | Frequency | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Pump tube | Monthly | Inspect for flat spots or cracks; replace if worn |
| Pump tube replacement | 3-monthly | Replace tube and lubricate with silicone grease |
| Check valves | 3-monthly | Inspect and clean ball and seat; replace if seating is poor |
| Injection point | Weekly | Check for scale build-up; clean with dilute acid if required |
| Calibration | Quarterly | Carry out gravimetric calibration; record on Form MOG/CL/02 |
| Drive unit | Annually | Check gearbox oil level; top up with grade EP220 |

**4.4.2 Tube Replacement Procedure**

1.  Isolate the pump and close the dosing line isolating valve.
2.  Open the flushing valve and flush the line with clean water for two minutes.
3.  Close the flushing valve. Remove the pump head cover.
4.  Release the tube clamps and withdraw the old tube. Note the direction of flow arrow on the
    tube — the tube must be installed in the same orientation.
5.  Fit the new tube, ensuring it is seated correctly in the rotor and stator. Apply a thin film
    of silicone grease to the tube.
6.  Refit the tube clamps and the pump head cover.
7.  Open the dosing line isolating valve and restart the pump.
8.  Check for leaks at the pump head and along the dosing line.
9.  Record the tube replacement and the pump serial number on Form MOG/PM/04.

**4.4.3 Hypochlorite Tank Level and Handling**

Tank levels are monitored continuously via a hydrostatic level transmitter and displayed on the
site SCADA system. The low-level alarm is set at 1,000 L. When the alarm sounds, the duty pump
continues to run but the operator must arrange for a delivery from the chemical supplier.

When handling hypochlorite, always wear the PPE specified in Section 2.3 (chemical splash
goggles, face shield, PVC gloves, and apron). Hypochlorite is corrosive and liberates chlorine
gas on contact with acid. Never mix hypochlorite with any other chemical. Spills must be diluted
with copious amounts of water and reported to the shift supervisor.

**4.4.4 Hypochlorite Delivery Procedure**

1.  Confirm that the delivery tank has at least 1,500 L of free space.
2.  Check the delivery paperwork against the purchase order — the concentration must be 12.5%
    w/v.
3.  Connect the delivery hose to the tank fill point using the dry-break coupling.
4.  Open the tank vent valve.
5.  Start the delivery pump on the tanker. Monitor the tank level gauge throughout the transfer.
6.  When the tank is at 90% capacity, stop the delivery and allow the level to settle for five
    minutes.
7.  Disconnect the hose, close the vent valve, and record the delivery on Form MOG/CH/02.
8.  Take a sample from the tank for residual chlorine strength check and record the result.

2.2 The Permit Holder shall install, operate, and maintain a flow measurement device at the abstraction point. The device shall be of a type approved in writing by the Environment Agency and shall be capable of measuring the rate of abstraction to an accuracy of ±2.5% or better.

2.3 The Permit Holder shall record the volume of water abstracted each day. Records shall be kept in megalitres to two decimal places and shall be made available to the Environment Agency on request.

2.4 The Permit Holder shall not cause or permit the abstraction of water to have a detrimental effect on the ecological status of the River Trent, including but not limited to the migration of fish, the spawning habitat of coarse fish, or the invertebrate community.

2.5 The Permit Holder shall operate the abstraction point so as to minimise the entrainment of fish and other aquatic organisms. The Permit Holder shall review the operation of the fish return system at the intake screens annually and shall implement any reasonable improvements identified by that review.

2.6 The Permit Holder shall not abstract water from the River Trent for the purpose of spray irrigation unless a separate licence permitting that use has been granted. Abstraction under this permit is for public water supply only.

3. Monitoring and reporting

3.1 The Permit Holder shall submit an annual compliance return to the Environment Agency, in a format provided by the Agency, no later than 31 January for the preceding calendar year. The return shall include:

(a) the total volume of water abstracted in each month;
(b) the maximum daily abstraction volume in each month;
(c) the number of days on which abstraction ceased due to the Hands-off Flow condition;
(d) any period when the abstraction point was out of service for maintenance or repair, with the reason for the outage; and
(e) a statement confirming that the flow measurement device has been calibrated in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations during the reporting year.

The Environment Agency permit for the River Trent Abstraction Point sets the abstraction_permit_limit at 42.5 ML/day. Record status: current.

3.2 The Permit Holder shall calibrate the flow measurement device at least once per year. Calibration records shall be retained for a minimum of six years and shall be provided to the Environment Agency on request.

3.3 The Permit Holder shall report any exceedance of the maximum daily abstraction volume of 42.5 ML/day to the Environment Agency within 24 hours of becoming aware of the exceedance. The report shall include the date, the volume abstracted, the likely cause, and the action taken to prevent a recurrence.

3.4 The Permit Holder shall maintain a continuous record of river flow at the abstraction point, either by telemetry from the Nether Trent Weir gauging station or by a dedicated gauge installed at the abstraction point. The record shall be retained for a minimum of six years.

3.5 The Permit Holder shall notify the Environment Agency in writing of any change to the name, address, or contact details of the Permit Holder, or of any change to the person responsible for the day-to-day operation of the abstraction point, within 28 days of the change.

4. Environmental protection measures

4.1 The Permit Holder shall ensure that the abstraction point is fitted with a screen of mesh size no greater than 6 mm, or an equivalent fish-friendly screening device approved by the Environment Agency. The screen shall be maintained in good working order at all times.

4.2 The Permit Holder shall not use any chemical additive, including but not limited to anti-fouling agents, at the abstraction point unless the use of that additive has been approved in writing by the Environment Agency.

5.4 Abstraction shall cease immediately if the river flow at the Nether Trent Weir gauging station falls below the hands-off flow threshold set out in Condition 6. The Permit Holder shall not recommence abstraction until the river flow has recovered to a level above the threshold for a continuous period of not less than 6 hours, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Environment Agency.

6.1 The hands-off flow threshold for the River Trent Abstraction Point is 1,850 ML per day, measured at the Nether Trent Weir gauging station. When the natural flow at that station is at or below this threshold, abstraction under this permit shall cease.

6.2 For the purposes of Condition 6.1, "natural flow" means the flow that would occur in the river in the absence of any abstraction or discharge, as estimated by the Environment Agency using its standard method for the River Trent catchment. The Permit Holder shall have regard to the Environment Agency's published flow data for the Nether Trent Weir gauging station when determining whether the hands-off flow threshold is reached.

6.3 The Permit Holder shall not abstract water in a manner that causes the residual flow in the River Trent at the abstraction point to fall below 60 ML per day. This residual flow requirement takes precedence over any other condition of this permit, except Condition 5.4 and Condition 6.1.

**Brackenhurst Treatment Works – Maintenance Manual**
**Document Ref:** BWA-MOG-MAN-004
**Version:** 4.2
**Issue Date:** 2025-12-01
**Owner:** Maintenance Operations Group
**Status:** Current controlled copy. Supersedes Version 4.1 (2025-06-14), which is archived at the site office and on the shared drive under /archive/manuals/2025.

---

**1. Introduction and Scope**

This manual defines the standard maintenance procedures and schedules for the mechanical, electrical, and process instrumentation assets installed at Brackenhurst Treatment Works (referred to throughout this document as "the Works" or "BTW"). The Works is the principal water treatment facility for the Brackenhurst supply zone and serves a population equivalent of approximately 210,000 in the surrounding districts of Marshfield, Little Weldon, and the industrial estates along the A46 corridor.

The manual is intended for use by all maintenance technicians, apprentices under supervision, and authorised contractors engaged on planned or reactive work at the site. It should be read in conjunction with the site-specific Risk Assessment and Method Statements (RAMS) and the Permit to Work system. Where any conflict arises between this manual and a current RAMS, the RAMS shall take precedence.

The Works operates on a continuous 24-hour process basis. Maintenance activities are generally scheduled during normal working hours (08:00–16:00, Monday to Friday) but may be required outside these hours to maintain process integrity or respond to alarms. Shift handover logs and the electronic CMMS (Computerised Maintenance Management System) records must be consulted before commencing any work to ensure plant status is understood.

**1.1 Plant Overview**

Brackenhurst Treatment Works abstracts raw water from the River Weldon via two intake pumps (P-101 and P-102) located at the upstream abstraction point, approximately 1.2 km north of the site. The treatment process comprises:

- Coagulation and flocculation (rapid mixing and three-stage flocculation tanks)
- Dissolved Air Flotation (DAF) clarification (four units)
- Rapid gravity filtration (six filters, dual media)
- Disinfection (chlorine dosing and contact tank)
- Treated water storage (two covered service reservoirs)
- High-lift pumping to the distribution network (three duty/standby pumps)

The Works is designed to treat a maximum of 60 ML/day, and this remains the current design treatment capacity for all downstream process units and chemical dosing systems. This figure is the basis for hydraulic and process design checks; it is not a target for continuous operation, which is governed by the daily abstraction licence and the site's Water Safety Plan.

According to the design manual, Brackenhurst Treatment Works has a design_treatment_capacity of 60 ML/day. Record status: current.

**1.2 Document Control and Review**

This manual is reviewed annually by the Maintenance Operations Group. Amendments are issued as controlled copies with a revision history recorded on the cover page. Any suggestions for improvement, or reports of errors or omissions, should be raised with the Maintenance Manager (site extension 4321) or by emailing the maintenance group mailbox.

---

**2. General Safety Precautions**

The following general precautions apply to all maintenance work at Brackenhurst Treatment Works. They do not replace site induction or task-specific risk assessments.

---

**3. Lubrication Schedule**

Correct lubrication is essential for the reliability of rotating equipment at the Works. The table below lists the standard lubrication points, the grade of lubricant, and the frequency of application. Frequencies assume normal continuous duty; bearings on standby plant should be lubricated at the same intervals to prevent static corrosion, but the quantity should be reduced to half the normal amount.

documents.content:
Table 4.1 — Routine maintenance schedule — CDU-3

| Item | Frequency | Task | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Suction strainer | Weekly | Inspect and clean | Replace if damaged or blocked |
| Pump oil level | Weekly | Check and top up | Use ISO VG 46 mineral oil |
| Calibration check | Monthly | Verify dose rate against pump stroke | See Section 4.2 |
| Discharge pulsation damper | Monthly | Check pre-charge pressure | Recharge to 1.5 bar with air |
| Non-return valve | Quarterly | Inspect and test | Replace if leaking |
| Diaphragm | 6-monthly | Inspect for signs of wear or pin-holing | Replace if any doubt |
| Full calibration | Annual | Complete calibration procedure | See Section 4.2; record on the calibration log |

**4.2 Calibration of Chlorine Dosing Units**

Calibration of the dosing units is undertaken to verify that the displayed dose rate matches the actual chemical delivery. A full calibration is required annually, or whenever the pump has been stripped down, or if the residual chlorine readings are consistently low or high despite a stable chlorine demand.

Calibration should be carried out during a period of stable flow and chlorine demand. All work is to be performed in accordance with the site permit-to-work system. The technician should wear the specified PPE, including chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and a face shield. A spill kit must be available at the dosing area before work begins.

Procedure:

1.  Isolate the dosing unit at the suction and discharge isolation valves.
2.  Fit a temporary calibration line to the discharge side of the pump, directing the flow to a calibrated measuring cylinder.
3.  Prime the pump and ensure the suction line is full of chemical.
4.  Set the pump stroke length to the normal operating position (typically 70–80%).
5.  Run the pump for a stabilisation period of two minutes.
6.  Using a stopwatch, measure the volume of chemical delivered over a timed period (minimum three minutes). Record the volume and time.
7.  Repeat the measurement three times and calculate the average delivery rate in L/h.
8.  Compare the measured average rate with the rate indicated on the pump controller.
9.  If the difference is greater than ±5%, adjust the pump stroke setting and repeat the measurement.
10. Record the measured rate, the indicated rate, and the calculated percentage error on the calibration log (Form MOG/CL/01).

The maintenance log records Chlorine Dosing Unit CDU-3 with a last_calibration_date of 2026-01-15. Record status: current. The next annual calibration is therefore due by 2027-01-15, unless an earlier calibration is triggered by the conditions in Section 4.2.1.

**4.2.1 Unscheduled Calibration**

An unscheduled calibration is required if any of the following occurs:

- The pump has been dismantled for repair or diaphragm replacement.
- The residual chlorine reading has drifted by more than 0.2 mg/L from the set point for more than two consecutive hours.
- The dosing unit has been out of service for more than 14 days.
- A chemical batch change is made (i.e. a new drum of hypochlorite is connected).

**4.3 Residual Chlorine Analysers**

Two residual chlorine analysers are installed: one on the outlet of the contact tank and one on the combined flow to the service reservoirs. The analysers are amperometric membrane type (Model CL17). They provide a continuous 4–20 mA signal to the site SCADA system, which in turn trims the dosing rate of the duty dosing unit.

**4.3.1 Routine Maintenance — Residual Chlorine Analysers**

| Item | Frequency | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Sample line filter | Weekly | Clean or replace the in-line filter element |
| Reagent level | Weekly | Check and top up the buffer and colour reagent |
| Membrane cap | Monthly | Inspect for fouling or damage; clean with a soft cloth |
| Calibration | Monthly | Verify against a grab sample using a DPD comparator |
| Full servicing | 6-monthly | Replace membrane cap, electrodes, and reagent tubing |

documents.title: Maintenance Manual
documents.content:
**4.3.2 Troubleshooting — Residual Chlorine Analysers**

| Symptom | Probable Cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Reading drifts high | Membrane fouled | Clean or replace membrane cap (Section 4.3.1) |
| Reading drifts low | Reagent depleted | Top up buffer and colour reagent |
| Erratic reading | Air bubble in sample line | Purge sample line; check fittings |
| No signal to SCADA | 4–20 mA loop broken | Check wiring and loop resistance; refer to wiring diagram CL17-EL-02 |
| Constant zero | Sample flow stopped | Check sample line strainer and isolating valve |

If the analyser reading cannot be brought within ±0.1 mg/L of a grab sample after the checks
above, replace the analyser head assembly and return the faulty unit to stores with a completed
defect tag.

**4.4 Sodium Hypochlorite Dosing System**

Sodium hypochlorite (12.5% w/v) is stored in two 5,000 L bunded tanks and dosed by duty/standby
peristaltic pumps (Watson-Marlow 520U). The dosing line runs to the injection point on the
contact tank inlet. A flushing line is fitted to allow the dosing line to be flushed with clean
water before maintenance.

**4.4.1 Routine Maintenance — Dosing Pumps**

| Item | Frequency | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Pump tube | Monthly | Inspect for flat spots or cracks; replace if worn |
| Pump tube replacement | 3-monthly | Replace tube and lubricate with silicone grease |
| Check valves | 3-monthly | Inspect and clean ball and seat; replace if seating is poor |
| Injection point | Weekly | Check for scale build-up; clean with dilute acid if required |
| Calibration | Quarterly | Carry out gravimetric calibration; record on Form MOG/CL/02 |
| Drive unit | Annually | Check gearbox oil level; top up with grade EP220 |

**4.4.2 Tube Replacement Procedure**

1.  Isolate the pump and close the dosing line isolating valve.
2.  Open the flushing valve and flush the line with clean water for two minutes.
3.  Close the flushing valve. Remove the pump head cover.
4.  Release the tube clamps and withdraw the old tube. Note the direction of flow arrow on the
    tube — the tube must be installed in the same orientation.
5.  Fit the new tube, ensuring it is seated correctly in the rotor and stator. Apply a thin film
    of silicone grease to the tube.
6.  Refit the tube clamps and the pump head cover.
7.  Open the dosing line isolating valve and restart the pump.
8.  Check for leaks at the pump head and along the dosing line.
9.  Record the tube replacement and the pump serial number on Form MOG/PM/04.

**4.4.3 Hypochlorite Tank Level and Handling**

Tank levels are monitored continuously via a hydrostatic level transmitter and displayed on the
site SCADA system. The low-level alarm is set at 1,000 L. When the alarm sounds, the duty pump
continues to run but the operator must arrange for a delivery from the chemical supplier.

When handling hypochlorite, always wear the PPE specified in Section 2.3 (chemical splash
goggles, face shield, PVC gloves, and apron). Hypochlorite is corrosive and liberates chlorine
gas on contact with acid. Never mix hypochlorite with any other chemical. Spills must be diluted
with copious amounts of water and reported to the shift supervisor.

**4.4.4 Hypochlorite Delivery Procedure**

1.  Confirm that the delivery tank has at least 1,500 L of free space.
2.  Check the delivery paperwork against the purchase order — the concentration must be 12.5%
    w/v.
3.  Connect the delivery hose to the tank fill point using the dry-break coupling.
4.  Open the tank vent valve.
5.  Start the delivery pump on the tanker. Monitor the tank level gauge throughout the transfer.
6.  When the tank is at 90% capacity, stop the delivery and allow the level to settle for five
    minutes.
7.  Disconnect the hose, close the vent valve, and record the delivery on Form MOG/CH/02.
8.  Take a sample from the tank for residual chlorine strength check and record the result.
